name: The Baron and Others Attempt to Save the Burning Barn
description: A barn burns fiercely under the night sky, flames roaring and casting a bright glow across the field. The Baron, the steward, the steward's wife, the pastor, and several others rush to the scene, moving frantically through the smoke and heat. They carry buckets, pull on hoses, and shout directions, trying to douse the flames and salvage what they can. Despite their efforts, the fire spreads too quickly, consuming the structure. The group stands back, silhouetted against the blaze, watching as the barn collapses into embers.
related_events: Barn fire rages while onlookers attempt rescue efforts

name: Liesl, Georg, and Ferdinand Watch Flames from the Window
description: Liesl, Georg, and Ferdinand stand together at the window of the children's bedroom, their faces lit by the flickering glow of flames. Outside, fire spreads in the distance, casting shifting light across the room. They remain silent, eyes fixed on the burning scene beyond the glass.
related_events: Children and adults observe flames from bedroom window

name: Pastor Finds Dead Bird on Desk
description: The pastor enters his office and walks to his desk. He reaches to set down his briefcase and notices a dead bird lying in the center of the desk, its wings spread wide. His letter-opener is embedded in the bird's neck, the hilt protruding from its beak.
related_events: Pastor enters office and approaches desk
Pastor discovers dead bird on desk
Dead bird found with letter-opener embedded in neck

name: Searching the House for Hansi
description: The schoolteacher, the steward, and the steward's wife move through the midwife's house, calling out, 'Hansi!' and 'Hello, Hansi, where are you?' Their voices echo faintly in the dim light cast by the closed shutters. Room by room, they search, finding no trace of the boy. In the midwife's bedroom, the schoolteacher notices a photograph on display: it shows the doctor, an unknown woman, and Xenia as a small child. The three meet again in the stairwell, saying nothing at first, their silence confirming what each already knows.
related_events: Schoolteacher, steward, and steward's wife search house for Hansi
Schoolteacher discovers photo in midwife's bedroom
Searchers reunite in stairwell after failing to find Hansi

name: The Schoolteacher and the Steward Depart
description: The schoolteacher, the steward, and the steward's wife came out from behind the house. They walked down the path, left the property, and went their separate ways on the street. The house remained behind them, empty and with shutters closed.
related_events: Schoolteacher and steward with wife leave the property

name: Villagers Spread Rumors About the Doctor and the Midwife
description: After the schoolteacher, the steward, and his wife left the property and went their separate ways, the village grew restless. In the weeks that followed, people gathered in hushed groups, whispering about the doctor and the midwife. Some said the doctor was Hansi's father, and that he and the midwife had tried to end the pregnancy to hide their secret, which was why the child was born with a disability. Others began to question the circumstances of the doctor's wife's death, muttering that there was something suspicious about it, and that the doctor and the midwife might have had a hand in it. The rumors spread from house to house, growing with each telling, while the empty house with its closed shutters stood silent.
related_events: Village gossip spreads rumors about the doctor and midwife

name: The Pastor Removes the Ribbons
description: Outside, under the bright sunlight, the family gathers around the decorated Christmas tree. The pastor gently takes the white ribbon from Marie's head and the one from Martin's arm. He tells Marie she is now accepted as a full member of the church community and will receive Christ's body in bread and wine. To Martin, he says the nightly restraints are no longer needed, and that he is trusted to uphold mental and physical purity in the coming year. The children bow their heads, then kiss the pastor's hand. Their mother steps forward and embraces them both warmly.
related_events: Pastor removes white ribbon from Marie and Martin
Pastor declares Marie's acceptance into church community
Pastor releases Martin from nightly restraints
Pastor expresses trust in Marie and Martin for the new year
Children kiss Pastor's hand
Mother embraces Marie and Martin
related_occasions: Confirmation Preparation Ceremony

name: Franz and Matti at the Sawmill
description: Franz steps carefully into the ramshackle sawmill beside the river, moving slowly across the creaking wooden planks. Matti, standing nearby, points to the spot where the accident happened. 'There. Be careful. Everything's rotten here,' he says. Franz looks down through the floorboards at the saw below. He steps back and turns to Matti. 'Who made her climb up here?' he asks. Matti shifts uneasily. 'I haven't a clue. They told us to collect all the loose ends. She just climbed up there.' Franz frowns. 'She could never stand heights. It made her dizzy. Who assigned you to this job?' Matti replies, 'You know how it works. The sawmill needed to be cleaned up, and the foremen pick the weaker harvesters.' Franz stares at him. 'Who picked her?'
related_events: Franz cautiously approaches the accident site in the sawmill
Matti shows Franz the location of the accident at the sawmill
Franz expresses concern about the woman's fear of heights
Franz questions Matti about who made the woman climb to the accident site
Matti explains that the foremen assigned weaker harvesters to clean the sawmill

name: The Letter and the Memory of a Winter Night
description: In mid-December, the schoolteacher receives a letter from Eva. She writes that her father has found her a new job in the district capital, where she will begin work at the start of the New Year. The letter brings back the memory of the night she came to the school seeking shelter. It was cold, and she had appeared after dark, asking for a place to stay. They sat together in the schoolroom and talked through the night, sharing the story of their lives up to that point. The school holidays lasted until the day after New Year's, but on the second day after Christmas, under a bright and sunny sky, the schoolteacher sets out on foot toward Obersdorf to visit Eva and her parents.
related_events: Schoolteacher receives letter from Eva in mid-December
Eva seeks shelter at the school during a night visit
Schoolteacher and Eva share life stories through the night

name: The Schoolteacher's Visit to Obersdorf
description: In the cold, clear days after Christmas, the schoolteacher set out on foot toward Obersdorf. Snow covered the ground, broken only by the faint tracks of a carriage. He walked with a rucksack on his back, moving steadily through the quiet winter landscape. His path led him toward the district capital, where Eva and her parents lived. He continued on, following the road through the snow, until he reached the village.
related_events: Schoolteacher walks through snowy terrain toward the district capital
Schoolteacher travels to Obersdorf to visit Eva and her parents

name: The Snowfall at the Reformation Feast
description: Heavy snow blanketed the village at the start of November, covering the ground in a deep, early winter frost. Inside the church, the children's choir sang a solemn hymn: '...us free from all misery, that has hit us now. That old evil enemy, is serious about it, great power and much deceit are his cruel armor, no one on earth resembles him...' Outside, the wind carried the sound through the quiet, snow-laden streets. The Reformation feast, held that Sunday, passed without the Baron's presence—a rare absence, as he had returned to the village alone and stayed away from the gathering.
related_events: Winter arrives early with heavy snowfall
Children's choir sings hymn inside church
related_occasions: Reformation Feast

name: The Baron's Absence at the Reformation Feast
description: On the first Sunday of November, the village gathered for the Reformation feast under a deep blanket of snow. The children's choir sang inside the church, their voices rising in harmony. The Baron, who had recently returned to the village alone and without his family, did not appear at the feast. His absence was noticed by many, as he had always attended in years past.
related_events: Baron returns without his family and skips Reformation feast
related_occasions: Reformation Feast

name: The Village Celebrates the Reformation Feast
description: The villagers gathered to celebrate the Reformation Feast. The schoolteacher stood before the children's choir, guiding their performance. The children sang with bright, eager voices, their arms adorned with white ribbons. Marie and Martin stood among them, wearing the same white ribbons on their sleeves.
related_events: Community celebrates the Reformation Feast
Schoolteacher conducts the children's choir
Children sing enthusiastically
related_occasions: Reformation Feast

name: Marie and Martin Wear the White Ribbon at the Reformation Feast
description: During the Reformation Feast, as the villagers gathered to celebrate and the schoolteacher led the children's choir in song, Marie and Martin stood among the crowd with white ribbons tied to their arms. The ribbons caught the eye of those nearby, a quiet but noticeable presence amid the festivities.
related_events: Marie and Martin wear the white ribbon on their arm
related_occasions: Reformation Feast

name: The Word Spreads in the Village
description: Rumors of war began to circulate through the village, moving quickly from house to house. One villager, standing in the square, was the first to say the word 'WAR' aloud. Another immediately stepped forward, contradicting him sharply. But despite the denial, the word took hold. People went about their tasks in silence, glancing at one another, the idea lingering in their thoughts. By evening, the possibility of war had settled into the air, unspoken yet present, as if it had always been there.
related_events: News of potential war spreads through the village
Villager speaks the word WAR for the first time
Speaker is contradicted after mentioning war
War becomes a persistent thought in the community

name: Narrator Requests Bicycle to Visit Eva in Town
description: The news of possible war spread quickly through the village, and the word itself, once spoken, lingered in everyone's thoughts. The narrator decided to go to town to speak with Eva about what they should do if war broke out. He went to the Baroness and asked to borrow the bicycle that Eva had used when she visited her parents. He planned to make the trip the following weekend, riding into town to see her.
related_events: Narrator decides to travel to town to discuss war plans with Eva
Narrator requests the bicycle from the Baroness
Narrator plans weekend bicycle trip to town

name: Paul Finds His Father in the Pigsty
description: Paul enters the pigsty and sees his father's body hanging from a hook on the wall, feet dangling above a knocked-over stool. He turns and runs out to the courtyard. He stops, then moves quietly back toward the stable door. His hand touches the door, but he does not go in. Slowly, he walks to the living room. The children are gathered there, unaware of him. Leni, who is cooking, glances up briefly. Paul sits down on a bench against the wall. The room is dark.
related_events: Paul discovers his father's body in the pigsty
Paul flees the stable after discovering the body

name: Paul Hesitates at the Stable Door
description: Paul runs from the stable into the courtyard and stops. He walks quietly toward the stable door and reaches out to touch it, but does not go inside. After a moment, he turns away and walks slowly toward the living room.
related_events: Paul hesitates at the stable door

name: Paul retreats to the living room
description: Paul turned away from the stable and walked slowly toward the living room. He entered the dim room and sat down on a bench against the wall. The children were gathered inside, but none of them looked at him. Leni, standing at the stove, glanced over briefly from her cooking, then returned to her work. Paul remained still, seated in the darkness.
related_events: Paul walks slowly to the living room
Leni briefly looks up from cooking
Paul sits on the bench in the dark living room

name: Villagers Search the Woods for Hansi
description: Under the dim light, villagers move through the trees, holding lanterns and torches aloft. They call out into the darkness: 'Hansi? Where are you? Give us a sign!' The voices repeat, growing clearer as figures emerge from the shadows. Men and women from the village draw nearer, scanning the area. One voice suddenly calls out, 'Over here. He's here.' Others rush forward toward a tree where a small boy is bound. They free him from his restraints, and he collapses. His head is wrapped in bloodied rags, a narrow slit left for breathing. A paper tied around his neck with a white ribbon bears words in block letters. No one speaks as the truth becomes clear—it is the midwife’s son.
related_events: Villagers search for Hansi in the dark with lanterns and torches

name: The Villagers Find the Boy Tied to the Tree
description: A figure among the trees catches someone's eye—a small boy bound tightly to a trunk, his head completely wrapped in bloodied rags, a narrow slit left open over his nose. A villager calls out, drawing the others. They hurry forward, lanterns and torches cutting through the dim light. One of them reaches the boy first, then others crowd in, untying the ropes that hold him. As the bindings fall away, the boy collapses. Hands carefully unwind the rags from his head, revealing a face streaked with blood. The midwife’s son—the boy with the still, distant eyes—lies unconscious before them. A paper hangs from his neck, fastened by a white ribbon, the words on it printed in bold, uneven letters.
related_events: Boy found bound to tree with head wrapped in rags
Villager discovers bound boy and calls for others
Villagers free bound boy from tree and unwrap his head

name: Unwrap the Boy and Read the Message
description: The villagers cut the ropes binding the boy to the tree. He collapses into their arms as they carefully unwind the bloodied rags from his head. Under the flickering light of lanterns and torches, they see his face and recognize him—he is the midwife’s son, the boy with the still eyes and soft features. Someone notices the paper tied around his neck with a white ribbon. A man takes it, unfolds it, and reads aloud in a trembling voice: FOR I THE LORD YOUR GOD AM A JEALOUS GOD, VISITING THE INIQUITY OF THE FATHERS UPON THE CHILDREN TO THE THIRD AND THE FOURTH GENERATION OF THOSE WHO HATE ME.
related_events: Boy identified as midwife's mongoloid son
Villager reads message on paper tied around boy's neck

name: Narrator Seeks the Baron After the Midwife's Disappearance
description: The midwife did not return. The narrator waited two days, then went to the manor house to inform the Baron. The Baron was there, and the narrator told him about the midwife. The Baron responded by directing the narrator to speak with the steward and instructed that the house be opened and the disabled boy taken care of.
related_events: Midwife fails to return and narrator waits for two days
Narrator travels to manor house to inform the Baron

name: The Baron Sends the Narrator to the Steward
description: The narrator went to the manor house to inform the Baron that the midwife had not returned. The Baron listened, then told the narrator to speak with the steward. He instructed the narrator to open the house immediately and to see to the care of the disabled boy.
related_events: Baron instructs narrator to open the house and care for the disabled boy

name: The Steward and Companions Break Into the House
description: The steward arrived at the house with his wife and the schoolteacher. He tried several keys in the lock, but none worked. After the attempts failed, the three of them forced open a door at the rear of the house and entered.
related_events: Steward attempts to unlock house with multiple keys
Steward, his wife, and the schoolteacher break down rear door of the house

name: Examine the Dead Horse by Torchlight
description: The steward held up a torch, casting a flickering glow over the dead horse lying on the ground. The landowner crouched beside the animal, inspecting the wounds on its front legs. The deep cuts on the pasterns were clearly visible in the torchlight. The steward watched as the landowner studied the injuries, then spoke about the horse’s damaged tendons and the wire tied at knee height in the trees.
related_events: Steward lights dead horse with torch
Landowner examines wounds on dead horse's front legs

name: The Steward Reports the Doctor's Injury
description: The steward told the landowner that the doctor had a broken collarbone and was in no condition to speak about what happened. He said he had asked the doctor’s daughter, but she did not know how the horse had been injured.
related_events: Steward reports doctor's injury and lack of communication
Steward learns daughter has no knowledge of incident

name: The Landowner Questions the Wire's Purpose
description: The landowner asked the steward about the wire. The steward replied that he had already checked it—it was thin but strong, nearly invisible unless looked for, and tied at knee height. The landowner wanted to know why it had been placed there. The steward shrugged, suggesting it might have been meant for children to jump over, though he doubted the doctor had put it there himself. He added that whoever did it had done so on purpose, and the setup looked strange.
related_events: Steward examines wire tied at knee height
Landowner questions purpose of wire
Steward speculates about intention behind wire placement

name: The Policeman Questions Witnesses After the Horse Accident
description: The policeman stands near one of the trees where a wire had been tied, examining the spot where it tripped the doctor's horse. He asks Xenia and the midwife who might have placed the wire and who took it away. Xenia says she was at school and did not see the wire. The midwife says she arrived at noon to prepare lunch, as she has done since the doctor's wife died four years earlier, and that she had not seen the wire before. The two boys, Rudolph and Hans, run through the garden and nearby fields, ignoring the questioning. Hans suddenly runs back, shouting for his mother. He leads her and the others to the edge of the field, where a group of people hurries along the path carrying a body on a makeshift stretcher. As they disappear into the bushes, the sound of their passage fades, leaving the scene in uneasy silence.
related_events: Wire trips the doctor's horse causing a fall
Policeman searches for clues at the tree where the wire was tied
Policeman questions Xenia and the midwife about the wire
Hans and Rudolph play in the garden and fields
related_occasions: Investigation Into The Doctor'S Horse Accident

name: Hans Alerts the Group to the Arrival of the Stretcher
description: Hans runs into the garden, shouting for his mother and urging her to come. He leads the midwife, the policeman, and Xenia toward the field, where a group of people is seen approaching along the path bordering the doctor's property. They carry a body on a makeshift stretcher. The group passes quickly, disappearing behind the bushes, their pace urgent. No one speaks as they watch the figures move away.
related_events: Hans alerts the midwife and others about approaching people
Group carries body on makeshift stretcher across the field
Policeman and Xenia follow the midwife toward the approaching group
related_occasions: Response To Tenant Farmer'S Wife'S Fatal Work Accident

name: Women Wash and Dress the Dead Woman
description: In a dim, low-ceilinged room with small windows, two women in peasant dresses lay the dead woman on the bed and begin to undress her. An elderly midwife, known for her role in bathing the dead, takes charge. They wash the body in silence. Each time the door opens, soiled water is carried out and fresh underclothes are brought in. Outside, villagers gather, their murmurs rising into louder, excited voices. The midwife drapes a dress over the body, leaving it half-covered. The farmer enters and tells her to leave. She hesitates, adjusts the dress, and exits with the others. The door closes. The farmer sits down beside his wife. He remains still for a long time, then tugs once at the dress, as if to cover her better. He sits motionless in the dark, his breath uneven, barely audible.
related_events: Women prepare the dead woman's body for burial
Midwife specialized in bathing oversees the body preparation
Soiled washing water is removed and fresh supplies are brought in
Villagers gather and mutter outside the room
Sounds of excited voices grow louder outside
related_occasions: Post-Mortem Body Preparation Ritual

name: The Farmer Interrupts the Bathing Ritual
description: The farmer enters the low-ceilinged room where the women are preparing his wife’s body. The old midwife turns and tells him to stay outside, but he quietly tells her to leave. She hesitates, drapes the dress over the half-naked body, and exits with the other women. After the door closes, the farmer remains standing for a long moment. Then he moves to the bed and sits beside his dead wife. He sits motionless for a long time, then reaches out once to tug at the dress, covering a patch of her skin. He stays beside her in silence, the sound of his uneven breathing the only sign of life in the dark room.
related_events: Farmer enters the room and interrupts the body preparation
Bathing-midwife protests and exits the room
Farmer sits beside his dead wife in silence
Farmer adjusts the dress to cover his wife's body
related_occasions: Post-Mortem Body Preparation Ritual

name: Sepp Looks at His Mother's Face
description: Sepp sneaks barefoot into the room where his mother's body lies on the bed, the candles beside it nearly burned out. He hesitates, then slowly moves closer. After pausing several times, he reaches out and lifts the white handkerchief covering her face. He stares at her, motionless, his mouth and eyes wide open. Suddenly, a noise breaks the silence. He flinches and pulls back, stepping away from the bed.
related_events: Sepp sneaks into the room where his mother's body is laid out
Sepp lifts the handkerchief to look at his mother's face
Sepp is startled by a noise and jerks back from the bed

name: Sepp Sees Paul and Sits Beside Him
description: Sepp turned around, startled by a sound, and saw his older brother Paul sitting on a bench against the wall. 'Pauli?!' Sepp whispered, his voice low and surprised. Paul did not answer. Sepp hesitated, then moved across the room and sat down beside him on the bench. They sat close together in the dim light, saying nothing.
related_events: Sepp notices his brother Paul sitting on a bench in the room
Sepp whispers to his brother Paul in surprise
Paul remains silent in response to Sepp
Sepp sits beside his brother Paul on the bench

name: Sepp Sits Beside Paul in the Silent Room
description: After hesitating by the bed, Sepp walks to the bench where Paul is sitting and sits down beside him. The two boys sit close together, not speaking, their bodies nearly touching. The room is dim, the candles nearly burned out, and no sound breaks the stillness.
related_events: Sepp and Paul sit close together in silence in the dark room

name: Narrator begins the story with hesitation and resolve
description: A man rides a dressage horse inside an enclosed arena. The camera captures close shots of his boots, spurs, whip, and the taut reins. The horse's mouth foams, its hooves thud against the ground, and the rider issues sharp commands. Its breath comes in loud snorts. Over these images, a quiet voice speaks. The voice admits not knowing whether the story is fully true, says much of it comes from hearsay, and acknowledges that many parts remain unclear. Despite this, the voice insists the events must be told, because they may shed light on what is happening in the country. Outside the arena, the rider leaves the stable on horseback. He passes through a gate and rides down a tree-lined path. The figure grows smaller as he moves into the distance, until he disappears from view. The voice continues, saying that everything began with the doctor's riding accident, after he finished his session and started home.
related_events: Narrator introduces uncertain account of village events

name: Doctor Rides Out After Dressage Session
description: A man rides a dressage horse inside the manor's riding school, his face hidden from view. The camera captures only his boots, spurs, whip, and the taut reins in his hands. The horse's mouth foams as it snorts, its hooves thudding against the ground in steady rhythm. The rider issues sharp, rapid commands, guiding the animal through precise movements. When the session ends, he steers the horse toward the open gate beside the camera, passes through, and rides into the avenue beyond. The stables recede behind him as he continues on, growing smaller in the distance until he disappears from sight.
related_events: Rider commands dressage horse during training session
Rider finishes dressage session and exits riding stables
Doctor rides toward home after training session

name: Narrator Recalls the Doctor's Riding Accident
description: The narrator speaks of the events that began in the village, stating that they started with the doctor's riding accident. After finishing his dressage session at the manor, the doctor had left the stables and ridden toward his home. Though the details of the accident are not yet known, the narrator marks this moment as where everything began.
related_events: Narrator recalls doctor's riding accident as narrative starting point

name: The Pastor Administers Communion to the Confirmation Candidates
description: The church is full. Eight young candidates kneel at the Communion bench, one after another. The pastor moves down the line, holding the cup to each child's lips. 'Accept and drink! This is the blood of the New Testament, shed for the forgiveness of your sins.' Each child drinks. When he reaches Marie, who is fifth in line, he pauses. The silence stretches. Some in the congregation glance with impatience. Marie sways slightly, her face pale. Then he offers her the cup. She drinks. He wipes the rim where her mouth touched, as he did for the others, and continues to the next child, repeating the words and the rite until all have received.
related_events: Pastor administers communion cup to confirmation candidates
related_occasions: Confirmation Ceremony At The Church

name: The Pastor Hesitates at Marie's Turn
description: The church is full, and the eight confirmation candidates are kneeling at the Communion bench. One by one, the pastor brings the cup to their lips. When he reaches Marie, the fifth in line, he stops. His pause stretches, long enough to draw uneasy glances from the congregation. Marie trembles, her face pale, her body taut as if she might collapse. The pastor remains still for another moment, then lifts the cup to her mouth. She drinks. 'Accept and drink! This is the blood of the new testament, shed for you so that your sins will be forgiven.' He wipes the rim of the cup and moves to the next candidate, continuing the rite as before.
related_events: Pastor hesitates before giving Marie the communion cup
Marie shows signs of fainting during the ceremony
Pastor offers communion cup to Marie despite hesitation
Marie drinks from the communion cup
related_occasions: Confirmation Ceremony At The Church

name: The Pastor Wipes the Cup and Continues the Communion
description: After Marie drank from the cup, the pastor wiped the rim where her mouth had touched, just as he had done for the others. He then moved to the next candidate, holding out the cup and saying the same words, and continued down the line until all eight had received communion.
related_events: Pastor wipes communion cup after Marie's use
Pastor continues communion rite with remaining candidates
related_occasions: Confirmation Ceremony At The Church

name: Rudolph Asks About the Dead Woman
description: Xenia and Rudolph sit in the kitchen eating in the dim light. After a long silence, Rudolph asks about the woman Xenia mentioned earlier. Xenia says the woman was dead. Rudolph does not understand and asks what dead means. Xenia tells him it means the person doesn’t live anymore. Rudolph asks when someone stops living. Xenia says it happens when people are too old or very ill. Rudolph wants to know about the woman, and Xenia explains she had an accident, that she was hurt very badly, worse than their father. Rudolph asks if that means she had to die. Xenia says yes, and that most people don’t die from accidents but much later, when they are very old. Rudolph pauses, then asks if all people die. Xenia says yes, everyone. Rudolph asks if Xenia will die. She says yes, everyone does, but not for a very long time. He asks if he will die too. She says yes, but not for a very long time. He asks if there is anything one can do to stop it. Xenia says no, it has to happen, but not now. After a long silence, Rudolph asks about their mother. He asks if she didn’t go on a trip. He then asks if she is dead too. Xenia says yes, she is dead, but it was a long time ago. They sit in silence as the kitchen grows dark. Suddenly, Rudolph sweeps his plate off the table with a sharp motion. It crashes to the floor. Xenia sits frozen. Then she begins to cry, quietly, turning away to hide it from him.
related_events: Rudolph asks about the meaning of death
Xenia explains death to Rudolph

name: Rudolph Asks About Death
description: Rudolph and Xenia sit in the kitchen eating in the dim light. After a while, Rudolph asks about the woman they encountered earlier. Xenia says the woman was dead. Rudolph wants to know what dead means, and Xenia explains that it means someone has stopped living. Rudolph asks when people stop living, and Xenia says it happens when they are too old or very ill. She tells him the woman died in an accident, something that hurt her so badly her body couldn’t go on. Rudolph thinks of their father and asks if it was like his injury. Xenia says yes, but much worse. Rudolph asks if everyone dies. Xenia says yes, everyone. He asks if she will die, and she says yes, and so will he, but not for a very long time. He asks if there is any way to stop it, and she says no, it has to happen, but not for a long while. Then Rudolph asks about their mother. After a pause, he asks if she is dead too. Xenia says yes, she died a long time ago. They sit in silence as the kitchen grows dark. Suddenly, Rudolph sweeps his plate off the table, shattering it on the floor, and turns away. Xenia sits still for a moment, then begins to cry, trying to hide it from him.
related_events: Rudolph inquires about the cause of the woman's death
Xenia clarifies that death is inevitable for everyone

name: Rudolph Learns About His Mother's Death
description: After a long silence, Rudolph asks if their mother went on a trip. He pauses, then asks if she is dead too. Xenia says yes, she is dead, but that it happened a long time ago. The kitchen has grown dark. Suddenly, Rudolph knocks his plate off the table with a sharp motion. The plate hits the floor and shatters. Xenia sits frozen for a moment. Then she begins to cry, quietly, turning away to hide her tears from him.
related_events: Rudolph questions whether his mother went on a trip
Rudolph expresses anger by knocking his plate off the table
Xenia begins to sob after Rudolph's outburst

name: The Doctor's Fall After the Horse Trip
description: The doctor's horse trips over a taut wire stretched between two trees as it enters the property. The doctor is thrown from the saddle and lands hard on the ground. He lies motionless, his arm twisted at an unnatural angle, a visible bump under his blood-soaked jacket where his collarbone is broken. He cries out in pain. The horse, injured and twitching, remains on the ground nearby.
related_events: Horse trips over taut wire strung between trees
Doctor suffers injuries after fall from horse

name: Xenia Runs to Her Father After the Fall
description: Xenia, the doctor's twelve-year-old daughter, comes running from the house after seeing the accident. She rushes to her father, who lies on the ground with his arm twisted and a bloody jacket, and stares at him in horror. Her eyes dart to the horse, twitching beside him. She screams. The doctor shouts something through his pain. She bends down, tries to lift him, but he cries out, and she stumbles back, helpless. He shouts again, and she turns and runs away.
related_events: Xenia discovers her injured father and wounded horse
Doctor shouts instructions to Xenia while in pain

name: Xenia Tries to Help Her Father
description: Xenia bends over her father and reaches to help him up, but he cries out in pain, causing her to stumble backward. She stands frozen for a moment, then turns and runs away across the field.
related_events: Xenia attempts to help her father stand
Xenia runs off after receiving second instruction

name: Xenia Seeks Help After the Accident
description: Xenia sees the accident from the window and runs to alert a woman from a neighboring house. The neighbor then carries the message to the manor house. Soon after, help arrives and the injured doctor is taken away to the hospital in the district capital.
related_events: Xenia observes accident from house window and alerts neighbor
Neighbor relays message to manor house for help
Injured doctor is transported to district capital hospital

name: Rudolph Searches for Xenia at Night
description: Rudolph comes down the stairs in the dark, wearing a nightshirt. The only light comes from the living room. He calls softly, 'Xeni?' The living room is empty. On the stairway, he notices a glow beneath the door of the practice room. He goes down again and opens the door. Inside, the doctor and Xenia sit facing each other in the bright light. The doctor has his back to Rudolph. Xenia is on the visitor's chair, her face tearstained. The doctor's legs are closed around hers. She looks up, startled. 'Rudi?!' The doctor spins around, stunned. 'What are you doing here?' Xenia asks. 'Why aren't you in bed?' Rudolph says, 'I can't get to sleep.' 'That's why you're wandering around like a ghost?' 'I woke up and you weren't there.' She wipes her face. 'Dad has pierced my earlobes.' 'Does it hurt?' 'Yes, a bit.' 'That's why you're crying?' 'I'm not crying anymore.' The doctor stands, walks to a closet, puts something inside, straightens his clothes. 'Now go to bed again. You too, Xeni.' 'Yes,' she says. Rudolph hesitates, watching her. 'I haven't worn earrings for a long time,' she says, almost eagerly. 'My earlobes grew back. For Whitsun, I'm getting new ones. Mom's garnet earrings.' She touches one ear. Rudolph looks at her. name: Marie and Martin Return Home Late
description: Marie and Martin come through the door and stand in front of it. At the dinner table, the pastor sits with his back to the door, his wife Anna seated across from him. I don't know what's worse: your absence or your coming back.' He pauses. 'Tonight we shall all go to bed hungry.' He stands. Anna and the children rise. The pastor turns to Marie and Martin. 'You probably agree with me that I cannot leave your offense unpunished, if we are to keep living in mutual respect. Tomorrow evening at this hour, I shall give each of you ten strokes of the cane. Until then, you have time to ponder over your offense. Do you agree with me?' Marie and Martin say, 'Yes, Father.' 'All right then. Go to bed now, all of you.' The children at the table go to their mother, then to their father, kiss their hands, and leave. As Marie and Martin move to do the same, the pastor says, 'I refuse to be touched by you. Your mother and I will sleep poorly because we know I have to hurt you tomorrow, and because it will be more painful to us than the strokes will be to you. Leave us alone and go to bed.'

name: The Baroness Announces She Will Leave with the Children
description: After the meal, the maid cleared the table and left with the tray. The Baron stood with his back to his wife, pouring himself a glass of brandy. He began speaking about timber from the birches in Aigen, estimating the volume and the time it would take to finish the work. The Baroness interrupted him, saying she would not stay. The Baron turned, not understanding at first. She repeated that she would leave with the children. He asked what she meant, and she told him plainly that she was taking the children and leaving the estate. He demanded to know how she planned to do that. She replied quietly that she did not yet know, but they would leave. The Baron responded with sarcasm, saying 'We.' The Baroness held his gaze. The maid reentered to clear the rest of the table, causing a long pause. The Baron drank his brandy and went to the window, waiting. As the maid prepared to leave, the Baroness told her she was no longer needed and thanked her. The maid said good night to both and exited. They remained silent for a long time. The Baroness then said she had returned from Italy out of decency, to give them a chance. The Baron turned sharply, incredulous, asking if he had missed his chance. She asked if his sarcasm would help solve anything. He asked what problem needed solving. She looked at him, then rose to leave. He suddenly shouted for her to stay. She turned. He said more quietly that she would only leave the room when he allowed it. She said nothing, returned to her chair, and sat down. She told him she had wanted to spare him the truth, but he left her no choice. During their stay with Uncle Edoardo, she had fallen in love with a man from Lombardy who worked in banking and had helped her uncle with a financial matter. The man had courted her and been kind to the children. She credited him with Sigi’s healthy growth and improved spirits. Despite this, they had come back. She felt committed to the Baron. But she could no longer bear living there. It was not only for herself, though life with him was not fulfilling for a woman of her age. She was leaving because she did not want Sigi, and later the twins, to grow up surrounded by malice, envy, apathy, and brutality. The incident with Sigi’s whistle had been the final breaking point. He asks if they knew the doctor was leaving Eichwald. They say their mother told them, but Xenia had not mentioned it. He presses them, asking if Xenia said anything, and whether they ever wondered who might have harmed Hansi and Sigi, or set fire to the barn. Marie says they discussed it with their father, who believed it must have been a sick person. The schoolteacher continues questioning, reminding them that Sigi and Hansi were with them at Thanksgiving, but Marie responds with confusion, shaking her head. He asks what was done to them, and she looks at him, not understanding.

name: The Schoolteacher Questions Marie and Martin About Xenia
description: The schoolteacher sits with Marie and Martin in the pastor's living room after being invited in by the pastor's wife, who leaves to prepare coffee. He asks the children if they knew the Doctor was leaving Eichwald. Marie says no, but adds that their mother had told them when she came to pick them up. The schoolteacher looks at them with suspicion and says he feels they are hiding something. Marie asks what he means, but offers no further information. He presses them, asking again if Xenia gave no warning before leaving, but receives no answer.

name: The Schoolteacher Questions the Children About the Attacks
description: The schoolteacher turns to the children after the pastor's wife leaves to prepare coffee. He asks if they knew the doctor was leaving Eichwald. Marie says their mother told them, but Xenia had said nothing about it. The schoolteacher presses them, asking if Xenia gave any hint, but both children shake their head. He remarks it's unusual for a child not to mention such a thing, and suggests they might be hiding something. Marie looks confused. He then asks Martin again why they went to see Hansi. Marie answers they were worried because he was ill and his mother was gone. The schoolteacher insists he was asking Martin, but Martin only confirms the same. The schoolteacher shifts to the recent incidents. He asks who could have harmed Hansi, and then Sigi, who tied the wire in the doctor's garden, who set fire to the barn. Marie says they wondered about it too, and that they had spoken with their father. He told them it must have been a sick person. The schoolteacher pauses, then reminds them that Sigi and Hansi were with them at Thanksgiving. Marie looks at him, then at her brother, then back at the schoolteacher, shaking her head and shrugging as if she does not understand. He asks, 'What did they do to you?' Marie replies, 'Who?' The pastor's wife returns with coffee, but the schoolteacher does not continue. He sees he will get no further.

name: The Schoolteacher Seeks the Pastor's Counsel
description: The schoolteacher sat across from Marie and Martin, pressing them about Xenia’s sudden departure and the recent incidents in the village. The children offered little, their answers brief and guarded. When the pastor’s wife returned, she announced her husband had come home. The pastor entered, removing his coat, and greeted the schoolteacher with a nod. Without further delay, the schoolteacher asked to speak with him privately. The pastor gestured toward the study. Inside, the schoolteacher closed the door and said the midwife knew who was tormenting her son. The two men sat in silence for a moment, the weight of the statement settling between them.

name: The Schoolteacher's Accusation
description: The schoolteacher arrives at the pastor's house in the evening and finds the doctor's practice closed. He tells the pastor that the doctor and his children have disappeared. Sitting with the pastor, he begins to recount a series of events: the children were seen near the doctor shortly after his accident; they later went to the midwife's garden looking for her son, Hansi, who had been attacked; the steward's daughter had dreamed of Hansi being beaten before it happened. The schoolteacher hesitates, then mentions he now recalls Baron's son was last seen in the company of the doctor's children. The pastor grows uneasy, demanding if the schoolteacher is saying the children committed these acts. The schoolteacher does not answer directly but lowers his head slightly, his hands folding in his lap. The pastor rises, shaken, and moves to close the windows of the house, one by one.

name: Pastor Confronts and Expels Schoolteacher After Accusations
description: The schoolteacher sits with the children in the living room, questioning them about Xenia, Hansi, and Sigi. He presses them on whether they know who might have harmed the boys or set the fire. Before they can answer, the pastor enters, having returned from church. He listens in silence as the schoolteacher continues to suggest the children may be hiding something. The pastor’s expression darkens. He steps forward, his voice trembling at first, then firm. He tells the schoolteacher his accusations are monstrous, that no child in his home will be treated as a suspect. He calls the questions immoral, the act of a man who has lost his way. He warns the schoolteacher that if such claims are repeated outside this house, he will face legal consequences. He questions the schoolteacher’s integrity, his role as an educator, and his presence in the community. Without waiting for a reply, the pastor orders him to leave and never return. The schoolteacher rises, hesitates, then walks out. The door closes behind him.
